# Uposathakkhandhaka (Kd 2)

**ID:** Kd 2
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Uposathakkhandhaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The chapter on the observance day
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd2
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uposathakkhandhaka* is the second chapter of the Khandhaka section of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka (traditionally forming part of the *Mahāvagga*) [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983; Banerjee 1979]. It sets out the regulations governing the monastic observance day (*uposatha*), held fortnightly on the new-moon and full-moon days, when the *Pātimokkha* is formally recited by an assembled quorum of four or more resident monastics [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009]. In addition to the recital procedures, the chapter contains the Buddha's permission to recite the code and the opening exhortation of the *Pātimokkha* accompanied by portions of the embedded Old Commentary (*padabhājaniya*), which later commentators such as Buddhaghosa incorporated into works like the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī* [Norman 1983]. Alongside the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka*, the text is one of the foundational treatises on communal legal acts (*saṅghakamma*) in the Vinaya; it details the formal communal boundaries (*sīmā*) delineating local monastic jurisdictions, as well as provisions for amending offenses and an extensive enumeration of fifty cases of non-offense [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009; Norman 1983].

In later literature and internal cross-references, the chapter is referred to under the designation *uposathasamyutta* in the *Sattasatikakkhandhaka* (Kd 22), reflecting early variability in chapter designations [Kang-yuan Sung 1999]. Commentary on its boundary regulations forms the basis of the *Sīmākathā* section in Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* [Norman 1983]. SuttaCentral records full parallels across other early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, including the Sanskrit *Poṣadhavastu* (Mūlasarvāstivāda), Tibetan and Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda texts, as well as Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka observance chapters, alongside a resembling Mahāsāṅghika parallel [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly aligns the Pali text with the Sanskrit *Poṣadhavastu* and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001), while internally identifying extensive textual reuse with other procedural Khandhakas, particularly the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4), the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15), and sub-commentarial treatises such as the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
